effects.name: Latent parameter
effects.summary: Represents one prior-backed latent scientific quantity with explicit support and named parameter dimensions.
effects.description:
`LatentParameter` is the general prior-backed quantity primitive.
`UnknownParameter` remains an exact compatibility alias. It owns one
latent realization over named distinct-parameter and constraint axes;
`replication_dims` repeat that realization without creating additional
parameters. `constraint_dims` name vector components or matrix rows/columns.
Legacy combined `param_dims` and replication `batch_dims` remain supported.
MAP may summarize this latent
at one point, but that inference choice does not turn it into a point-valued
parameter.

The support, prior, parameter axes, and sharing identity are part of the model.
If the parameter is weakly identified, the remedy is an informative prior,
better experimental excitation, or a simpler model—not a hidden conversion to
optimizer state.

effects.name: Noise addition
effects.summary: Defines a Normal measurement distribution around a supplied mean; data binding separately determines whether the site is observed.
effects.description:
`NoiseAddition` is the scientific convenience effect for an additive Normal
measurement distribution. It delegates sampling to the same role-neutral
`RandomVariable.Normal` machinery. Its mean and standard-deviation inputs
broadcast to the configured sample dimensions. A concrete observation
conditions the generated sample site; without an observation, the same effect
produces a fresh realization.

The effect is stochastic, but it does not independently define a scientific
bias or other deterministic unknown. Those quantities should remain explicit
upstream components so that the model graph preserves their meaning.
effects.equation: y = μ + ε,  ε ~ Normal(0, σ²)
effects.dimension_rule: broadcast(mean, standard_deviation) -> sample; batch/event roles are declared explicitly or inferred from dimensioned inputs
